Header:
- Date: 2026-03-09
- Time: 10:00 AM PT
- Duration: ~45 minutes
- Attendees: Alex (AE), Samir (SE), Jules (Solutions), Maya (CSM) -- Priya (PM), Mark (Data Eng), Elena (SecOps), Daniel (Backend)

Summary:
Quick weekly sync on the finance pilot. Main focus: model selection, pinning to a version for stability, fallback/rollback plans, and next steps for benchmark artifacts and security review. Some fuzzy transcription around kernel/quantization words.

Transcript:
00:00 Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll keep to 45. Quick roll call, and then Samir will walk through the benchmark results we ran last week.
00:12 Priya (PM): Hi all, thanks. We've got a tight timeline to validate the model quality before our demo on the 20th, so excited to see the numbers.
00:18 Samir (SE): Cool, thanks. So quick context, we ran three candidate models from the Redwood catalog: rwd-small-1.7b, rwd-latency-gg-7b and rwd-std-13b, and then the v2.0 and v2.1 variants for rwd-std-13b. Note, the naming in the table may look slightly off because the export hit some truncation.
00:38 Mark (Data Eng): Quick question, do those names map to the ones in our trial dashboard? I want to make sure our pinning references the exact model id.
00:44 Samir (SE): Yes, each row has the full model id. We'll send the sheet again. The headline: v2.1 gave slightly better precision on the finance QA prompts and improved token efficiency because of a new quantization kernel -- sorry the transcriber wrote "quantize Asian kernel" in the note, which is wrong.
01:02 Daniel (Backend): Can you clarify "pinning"? If we pin to v2.1 in the pilot, what happens if v2.1 has a regression in a later infra rollout?
01:10 Jules (Solutions): Good question. Pinning means the request routing will prefer the pinned model id for that route/environment. We also recommend a fallback chain: pinned -> previous stable -> hosted-low-cost. So if v2.1 regresses we can roll back to v2.0 or fall back to a lower-cost hosted variant.
01:28 Priya (PM): What's the latency delta? Our SLA target is sub-250ms p50 and p95 under 500ms for the demo workload.
01:36 Samir (SE): For the 2-token median prompt set, v2.1 p50 was ~210ms, p95 around 420ms on our dedicated infra sim. v2.0 p95 was closer to 520ms. The 13b gives better quality but at higher 99th percentile tail. We'll share the chart.
01:56 Elena (SecOps): On the security side, we need to confirm encryption at rest, transit, and KMS ownership. Can we pin in a VPC with customer-managed KMS?
02:06 Alex (AE): Yes, for the private pilot we can do VPC/private control plane and integrate with your KMS, but we'll need the SecOps call to confirm the exact flow and any audit log requirements.
02:15 Elena (SecOps): Also need SOC2 scope and where audit logs sit.
02:18 Maya (CSM): We'll attach the SOC2 summary and audit log retention options after the call.
02:23 Mark (Data Eng): Back to pinning: What about continuous batching and KV cache behavior when we pin across mixed workloads?
02:30 Samir (SE): The runtime will still do batching; pinning is at model id routing level. KV cache invalidation is per model variant, so if you switch from v2.1 to v2.0 you lose some cache hits. That's why we recommend canary pinning for a small traffic slice first, and then full cutover. Also there's a subtlety where the transcriber shows "K V cash" instead of KV cache.
02:50 Priya (PM): For canary, what's a safe initial percentage?
02:55 Jules (Solutions): Typically 5-10% traffic for 24-72 hours to validate no regressions on your golden prompt set. If metrics look good, ramp to 50% then 100%. We can automate rollbacks on regression triggers like quality drop > 2% or latency p95 increase > 15%.
03:12 Daniel (Backend): Are those regression checks in the Redwood Console or do we need our own monitoring?
03:17 Samir (SE): Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and latency, per-route model dashboards, and a quality hooks API to submit your golden outputs for automated checks. We'll show a quick demo in the security deep-dive if you want.
03:30 Priya (PM): One regression scenario: hallucinations on invoice parsing prompts. Does pinning affect hallucination rate?
03:36 Samir (SE): It's model-dependent. v2.1 reduced hallucination on the invoice set by ~4% vs v2.0 in our sample, but we'll need your golden outputs to confirm on your distribution.
03:46 Elena (SecOps): Also need to know data retention for logs and whether content leaves our VPC. We can't allow unencrypted transcripts off-prem for the pilot.
03:55 Alex (AE): Noted. For Private deployments we can keep data in your VPC; for Dedicated we have contractual controls. We'll follow up with the SecOps checklist.
04:05 Priya (PM): Anything else on fallbacks? If the pinned model becomes unavailable, what's the automatic behavior?
04:11 Jules (Solutions): Automatic fallback goes to the next compatible model in your route policy. You can also set a hard-fail if you prefer, but for demo reliability we usually recommend soft-fallback to avoid outages.
04:23 Mark (Data Eng): About cost: pinning to 13b v2.1 increases per-token unit cost by roughly 1.6x vs the small model. We need a cost table to justify for our CFO.
04:33 Alex (AE): We'll include a cost table with token cost and expected monthly run-rate under your projected QPS.
04:38 Samir (SE): One more technical note: when people say "quantization" in the notes, there's different profiles. For finance parsing we used int8 profile A which seems to preserve numerics better. The transcriber munged it as "intate profile A" in one row.
04:55 Priya (PM): OK. Timeline check: we need pinned model and benchmark by next Friday if possible.
05:01 Alex (AE): We can do that. Samir, you pick up the benchmark run and we'll schedule the SecOps deep-dive.
05:06 Samir (SE): Yep. I'll run the 1k sample across the three candidates with pinned v2.1 and produce p50/p95/p99, regression checks vs golden outputs, and cost per token breakdown.
05:16 Elena (SecOps): Send over the SecOps pre-reqs. We need vendor contact, network diagrams, KMS provider, and SOC docs.
05:23 Maya (CSM): I'll send the pre-req checklist and the SOC2 summary after the call.
05:28 Priya (PM): Great. Anything else?
05:30 Alex (AE): Quick recap of next steps...
05:33 Alex (AE): Action items: Samir runs benchmark and shares sheet by 3/13, Alex sends pricing and pilot criteria today, Priya shares golden prompts by 3/11, Elena confirms KMS provider by 3/18, Maya sends SOC2 and SecOps checklist by EOD.
05:50 Priya (PM): Sounds good, thanks everyone.
05:53 Alex (AE): Thanks all, talk next week.
